qns_content.text: A silver sheet has an area of \( 1.5 \, \text{m}^2 \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is the increase in area when heated to \( 120^\circ \text{C} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
Why do blacksmiths heat an iron ring before fitting it onto a wooden wheel?

text_solutions: Heating causes thermal expansion (Section 10.5), increasing the ring’s diameter (\( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T \)), allowing it to fit over the wheel; it contracts upon cooling for a tight fit (Example 10.2).

qns_content.text: A gas occupies \( 4.2 \, \text{L} \) at \( 1.4 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 47^\circ \text{C} \). If the pressure is increased by \( 0.6 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature decreased by \( 20^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?
During vaporization, what does the supplied heat primarily do to the liquid?

options.text: Converts it to vapor without temperature change

text_solutions: During vaporization, the supplied heat (latent heat of vaporization) breaks intermolecular bonds to convert the liquid into vapor, without changing its temperature.

qns_content.text: What happens to the volume of an ideal gas if its temperature is doubled at constant pressure?

text_solutions: For an ideal gas at constant pressure, Charles’ Law states that volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature. If temperature doubles, volume doubles.

qns_content.text: What is the Celsius temperature equivalent to \( 400 \, \text{K} \)?

A silver rod of length \( 1 \, \text{m} \) at \( 10^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 110^\circ \text{C} \). If its cross-sectional area increases by \( 0.0076 \, \text{cm}^2 \), what was its original area? (\( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))

A \( 0.15 \, \text{kg} \) copper block at \( 200^\circ \text{C} \) is dropped into \( 0.9 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \) in a calorimeter of mass \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) (specific heat = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \)). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) gold block at \( 1500^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.6 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) copper calorimeter at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of gold = \( 134 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A gas at \( 3.5 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 77^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 4.5 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature drops to \( 27^\circ \text{C} \) and volume increases to \( 6 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?

A gas at \( 2.4 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 87^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 7 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature is lowered to \( 37^\circ \text{C} \) and pressure adjusted to \( 3 \, \text{atm} \), what is the percentage change in volume?

How much heat is required to convert \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -30^\circ \text{C} \) to steam at \( 120^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))
Which of the following correctly relates the coefficients of linear and area expansion?

options.text: Area coefficient is half the linear coefficient
Area coefficient is twice the linear coefficient
Linear coefficient is twice the area coefficient

text_solutions: The coefficient of area expansion is approximately twice the coefficient of linear expansion (\( \Delta A / A \approx 2 \alpha_l \Delta T \)), as area involves two dimensions.

qns_content.text: During the melting of ice at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \), why does the temperature remain constant despite heat being supplied?

options.text: Heat is used to change the state, not raise temperature

text_solutions: The heat supplied during melting (latent heat of fusion) is used to change the state from solid to liquid, overcoming intermolecular forces, not to increase temperature (Section 10.8).

qns_content.text: How much heat is required to raise \( 0.8 \, \text{kg} \) of aluminium from \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) to \( 75^\circ \text{C} \) if its specific heat capacity is \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \)?

How much heat is needed to convert \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) of mercury at \( -39^\circ \text{C} \) to liquid at \( 357^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of solid mercury = \( 140 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 0.12 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of liquid mercury = \( 140 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A copper rod of length \( 80 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 40^\circ \text{C} \) is cooled until its length decreases by \( 0.0136 \, \text{cm} \). What is the final temperature? (\( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))

How much heat is required to raise \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) of water from \( 15^\circ \text{C} \) to \( 85^\circ \text{C} \) and then convert \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) to steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) silver calorimeter initially at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), silver = \( 236 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

A \( 0.15 \, \text{kg} \) mercury block at \( 400^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium calorimeter at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of mercury = \( 140 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which temperature scale uses absolute zero as its starting point?

text_solutions: The Kelvin scale starts at absolute zero, the theoretical point where all molecular motion ceases, making it an absolute temperature scale.

qns_content.text: A gas at \( 1.9 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 67^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 6.5 \, \text{L} \). If the pressure is increased to \( 2.5 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature raised to \( 117^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?

How much heat is required to convert \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -15^\circ \text{C} \) to steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

A brass cube of side \( 15 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 35^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 135^\circ \text{C} \). What is the increase in its surface area if one face is \( 225 \, \text{cm}^2 \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
A steel disc of radius \( 25 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 130^\circ \text{C} \). What is the increase in its area? (\( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
How much heat is needed to melt \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) of lead at its melting point of \( 328^\circ \text{C} \)? (Latent heat of fusion of lead = \( 0.25 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))
A steel cube of side \( 20 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 125^\circ \text{C} \). What is the increase in volume? (\( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
A gas occupies \( 2.5 \, \text{L} \) at \( 1.2 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 37^\circ \text{C} \). If the pressure is doubled and temperature increased by \( 50^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?

A \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) iron block at \( 150^\circ \text{C} \) is dropped into \( 1.5 \, \text{kg} \) of water at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of iron = \( 450 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

What is the heat required to raise the temperature of \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) of copper from \( 30^\circ \text{C} \) to \( 80^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which of the following is true about the Celsius and Fahrenheit scales at the ice point?

text_solutions: At the ice point (freezing of water at standard pressure), Celsius is \( 0^\circ \text{C} \) and Fahrenheit is \( 32^\circ \text{F} \) (Section 10.3).

qns_content.text: A \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) iron block at \( 300^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.8 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 24^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) silver calorimeter at \( 24^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of iron = \( 450 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), silver = \( 236 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
What happens to the pressure of an ideal gas if its volume is halved and temperature is kept constant?

text_solutions: Boyle’s Law (Section 10.4) states \( P V = \text{constant} \) at constant temperature. If \( V_2 = V_1 / 2 \), then \( P_2 = 2 P_1 \), so the pressure doubles.

qns_content.text: Why can’t you open a tightly screwed metal lid until it’s heated in hot water?

text_solutions: Heating the metal lid causes it to expand due to thermal expansion, loosening its grip on the jar, which expands less if made of glass or remains unchanged if plastic.

qns_content.text: A \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) lead block at \( 500^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 26^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) brass calorimeter at \( 26^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of lead = \( 127.7 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), brass = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which process describes the direct transition from solid to gas observed in iodine?

text_solutions: Sublimation is the process where a substance transitions directly from solid to gas, as observed with iodine under certain conditions.

qns_content.text: What happens to the temperature of an ideal gas if its volume doubles at constant pressure?

text_solutions: Charles’ Law states that at constant pressure, \( V / T = \text{constant} \). If volume doubles (\( V_2 = 2V_1 \)), the absolute temperature doubles (\( T_2 = 2T_1 \)).

qns_content.text: A \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) brass block at \( 350^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 27^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) iron calorimeter at \( 27^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of brass = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), iron = \( 450 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
Why does water in a calorimeter reach a steady temperature when mixed with a hot object?

text_solutions: In calorimetry (Section 10.7), heat lost by the hot object equals heat gained by the water and calorimeter at thermal equilibrium, where no further heat transfer occurs.

qns_content.text: A \( 0.25 \, \text{kg} \) silver block at \( 150^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 1 \, \text{kg} \) of water at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium calorimeter at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of silver = \( 236 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium block at \( 160^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 1.2 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 28^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) lead calorimeter at \( 28^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), lead = \( 127.7 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

How much heat is needed to convert \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) of water at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \) to steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \)? (Latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))
What is the relationship between the Celsius and Kelvin scales?

text_solutions: The Kelvin scale is offset from the Celsius scale by \( 273.15 \), so \( T = t_C + 273.15 \) (Section 10.4), where \( T \) is Kelvin and \( t_C \) is Celsius.

qns_content.text: What is the Kelvin temperature equivalent to \( -23^\circ \text{C} \)?
What is the key difference between Celsius and Fahrenheit scales at the boiling point of water?

text_solutions: At the boiling point of water under standard pressure, the Celsius scale reads \( 100^\circ \text{C} \), while the Fahrenheit scale reads \( 212^\circ \text{F} \), reflecting different interval sizes and zero points.

qns_content.text: Which of the following is true about latent heat during a phase change?

options.text: It changes the state without changing temperature

text_solutions: Latent heat is the heat absorbed or released per unit mass during a phase change without a temperature change (Section 10.8.1, \( Q = m L \)).

qns_content.text: A \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium block at \( 120^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.8 \, \text{kg} \) of water at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) copper calorimeter at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A silver sphere of radius \( 8 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 70^\circ \text{C} \) is cooled to \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is the decrease in its volume? (\( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))

A steel rod has a length of \( 1 \, \text{m} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What will be its length at \( 120^\circ \text{C} \) if the coefficient of linear expansion of steel is \( 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \)?
How much heat is required to melt \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \) to water at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \)? (Latent heat of fusion = \( 3.33 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

How much heat is required to convert \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -20^\circ \text{C} \) to water at \( 10^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A brass ring has an inner diameter of \( 5 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \). To what temperature must it be heated to increase the diameter to \( 5.009 \, \text{cm} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
How much heat is required to vaporize \( 0.15 \, \text{kg} \) of nitrogen at \( -196^\circ \text{C} \)? (Latent heat of vaporization of nitrogen = \( 2.0 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

How much heat is required to convert \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -18^\circ \text{C} \) to water at \( 40^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) copper calorimeter initially at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A \( 0.05 \, \text{kg} \) gold block at \( 1200^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of gold = \( 134 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
What is the significance of the latent heat of fusion?

text_solutions: The latent heat of fusion is the heat required per unit mass to change a substance from solid to liquid at its melting point, reflecting the energy needed to break intermolecular bonds.

qns_content.text: A \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium block at \( 80^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 25^\circ \text{C} \). Calculate the final temperature. (Specific heat of aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A gas occupies a volume of \( 2 \, \text{L} \) at \( 27^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 1 \, \text{atm} \) pressure. What will be its volume at \( 127^\circ \text{C} \) if the pressure remains constant? (Use ideal gas law)

A metal cube has a volume of \( 1000 \, \text{cm}^3 \) at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \). What will be its volume at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \) if the coefficient of volume expansion is \( 5.4 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \)?

A \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) tungsten block at \( 250^\circ \text{C} \) is dropped into \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 18^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) silver calorimeter at \( 18^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of tungsten = \( 134 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), silver = \( 236 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A gas at \( 17^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 2.5 \, \text{atm} \) occupies \( 5 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature is raised to \( 67^\circ \text{C} \) and the volume is adjusted to \( 7 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?

A copper cylinder has a volume of \( 500 \, \text{cm}^3 \) at \( 50^\circ \text{C} \). What temperature must it be cooled to for the volume to decrease by \( 0.85 \, \text{cm}^3 \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which scale measures temperature relative to the freezing and boiling points of water with 180 intervals between them?

text_solutions: The Fahrenheit scale uses \( 32^\circ \text{F} \) for freezing and \( 212^\circ \text{F} \) for boiling of water, with 180 intervals (\( 212 - 32 = 180 \)) between these points.

qns_content.text: Which material is preferred as a coolant in radiators due to its high capacity to absorb heat?

text_solutions: Water is preferred as a coolant in radiators because of its high specific heat capacity, allowing it to absorb significant heat with minimal temperature rise.

qns_content.text: A \( 0.45 \, \text{kg} \) copper block at \( 200^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 1.1 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 23^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) brass calorimeter at \( 23^\circ \text{C} \). What is the final temperature? (Specific heat of copper = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), brass = \( 386 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
What is the primary factor affecting the volume expansion of a gas compared to solids and liquids?

text_solutions: Gases expand much more than solids and liquids due to their higher coefficient of volume expansion, which is temperature-dependent and significantly larger (Section 10.5).

qns_content.text: Which property of a material explains why sand heats up faster than water under the same sunlight?

text_solutions: Specific heat capacity determines how much heat is needed to raise the temperature of a material. Sand has a lower specific heat capacity than water, so it heats up faster.

qns_content.text: How much heat is required to raise \( 0.5 \, \text{kg} \) of water from \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) to \( 80^\circ \text{C} \) and then convert \( 0.2 \, \text{kg} \) of it to steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of vaporization = \( 2.256 \times 10^6 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

A gas at \( 300 \, \text{K} \) and \( 1 \, \text{atm} \) occupies \( 3 \, \text{L} \). If it is heated to \( 450 \, \text{K} \) while the volume is adjusted to \( 4.5 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?

A gas at \( 2.8 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 97^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 3.8 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature is raised to \( 147^\circ \text{C} \) and volume reduced to \( 2.5 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?

A steel plate has an area of \( 1.2 \, \text{m}^2 \) at \( 45^\circ \text{C} \). What is the decrease in area when cooled to \( 5^\circ \text{C} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
How much ice at \( 0^\circ \text{C} \) will melt if \( 16744 \, \text{J} \) of heat is supplied? (Latent heat of fusion of ice = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \))

A brass rod of length \( 2.5 \, \text{m} \) at \( 20^\circ \text{C} \) is heated to \( 220^\circ \text{C} \). If its cross-sectional area increases by \( 0.018 \, \text{cm}^2 \), what was its original area? (\( \alpha_l = 1.8 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which property of a substance determines the amount of heat required to change its temperature by \( 1^\circ \text{C} \) per unit mass?

text_solutions: Specific heat capacity (\( s \)) is defined as the heat required per unit mass to change the temperature by \( 1^\circ \text{C} \) (Section 10.6, \( s = \frac{1}{m} \frac{\Delta Q}{\Delta T} \)).

qns_content.text: A gas expands from \( 4 \, \text{L} \) to \( 6 \, \text{L} \) at constant pressure of \( 2 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature \( 300 \, \text{K} \). What is the new temperature if the volume is reduced back to \( 4 \, \text{L} \) at constant pressure?
A copper cube has a side length of \( 10 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 30^\circ \text{C} \). What is its volume at \( 130^\circ \text{C} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.7 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which law explains why the volume of a gas increases when its temperature rises at constant pressure?

text_solutions: Charles’ Law states that at constant pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature (\( V / T = \text{constant} \), Section 10.4).

qns_content.text: A gas at \( 3 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 27^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 4 \, \text{L} \). If the pressure is reduced to \( 1.5 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature raised to \( 177^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?
Which gas law relates pressure and volume when temperature is held constant?

text_solutions: Boyle’s Law describes the inverse relationship between pressure and volume of an ideal gas at constant temperature (\( P V = \text{constant} \)).

qns_content.text: A \( 0.3 \, \text{kg} \) lead block at \( 400^\circ \text{C} \) is placed in \( 0.7 \, \text{kg} \) water at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \) in a \( 0.1 \, \text{kg} \) aluminium calorimeter at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \). Find the final temperature. (Specific heat of lead = \( 127.7 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), aluminium = \( 900 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

A gas at \( 1.5 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 77^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 9 \, \text{L} \). If the pressure is reduced to \( 1 \, \text{atm} \) and temperature lowered to \( 27^\circ \text{C} \), what is the new volume?

A gas at \( 67^\circ \text{C} \) and \( 1.6 \, \text{atm} \) occupies \( 8 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature is reduced to \( 17^\circ \text{C} \) and volume adjusted to \( 6 \, \text{L} \), what is the final pressure?
Which statement is true about the ideal gas equation?

text_solutions: The ideal gas equation (\( PV = nRT \)) relates pressure, volume, and temperature for an ideal gas, where \( R \) is the universal gas constant and \( n \) is the number of moles.

qns_content.text: What process occurs when dry ice changes directly from solid to vapor?

text_solutions: Sublimation is the direct transition from solid to vapor without passing through the liquid state, as seen with dry ice (Section 10.8).

qns_content.text: A gas at \( 2 \, \text{atm} \) and \( 47^\circ \text{C} \) occupies \( 6 \, \text{L} \). If the temperature drops to \( -3^\circ \text{C} \) and pressure becomes \( 1.5 \, \text{atm} \), what is the new volume?
Why does a metal rod expand more than a glass rod for the same temperature increase?

options.text: Metals have a higher coefficient of linear expansion
Glass has a higher specific heat capacity

text_solutions: Metals have a higher coefficient of linear expansion (\( \alpha_l \)) than glass (Section 10.5, Table 10.1). For the same \( \Delta T \), \( \Delta L = L_0 \alpha_l \Delta T \) is greater for metals due to their larger \( \alpha_l \).

qns_content.text: Why does steam at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \) cause more severe burns than water at \( 100^\circ \text{C} \)?

text_solutions: Steam releases additional latent heat of vaporization when it condenses on skin, transferring more energy than liquid water at the same temperature.

(Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), iron = \( 450 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))

Why does a calorimeter use a material with low specific heat capacity for its container?

text_solutions: A material with low specific heat capacity absorbs less heat, minimizing its effect on the heat exchange between the substances being measured, ensuring accurate results.

Why do gases expand more than solids for the same temperature increase?

text_solutions: Gases have a much higher coefficient of volume expansion than solids due to weaker intermolecular forces, allowing greater volume changes with temperature.

Which temperature scale uses \( 32^\circ \) and \( 212^\circ \) as the freezing and boiling points of water at standard pressure?

text_solutions: The Fahrenheit scale defines the freezing point of water as \( 32^\circ \text{F} \) and boiling point as \( 212^\circ \text{F} \) at standard pressure (Section 10.3).

qns_content.text: What happens to the boiling point of a liquid when external pressure decreases?

text_solutions: Decreasing external pressure reduces the energy needed for molecules to escape into the vapor phase, lowering the boiling point, as seen in high-altitude cooking.

qns_content.text: A silver ring has an inner circumference of \( 31.4 \, \text{cm} \) at \( 15^\circ \text{C} \). What temperature must it be heated to for the circumference to increase by \( 0.0597 \, \text{cm} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.9 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which substance typically has the highest specific heat capacity among common materials?

text_solutions: Water has the highest specific heat capacity (\( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \)) among common substances listed (Section 10.6, Table 10.3), making it an effective coolant.

Which of the following is true about the coefficient of volume expansion compared to the coefficient of linear expansion?

text_solutions: The coefficient of volume expansion (\( \alpha_v \)) is three times the coefficient of linear expansion (\( \alpha_l \)), as \( \alpha_v = 3 \alpha_l \) (Section 10.5).

qns_content.text: A steel cylinder has a volume of \( 1.5 \, \text{L} \) at \( 55^\circ \text{C} \). What temperature must it be heated to for the volume to increase by \( 0.0054 \, \text{L} \)? (\( \alpha_l = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \text{K}^{-1} \))
What is the Fahrenheit temperature equivalent to \( 75^\circ \text{C} \)?
What happens to the volume of an ideal gas if its pressure is doubled while the temperature remains constant?

text_solutions: According to Boyle’s Law (Section 10.4), for an ideal gas at constant temperature, \( P V = \text{constant} \). If pressure doubles (\( P_2 = 2P_1 \)), then \( V_2 = V_1 / 2 \), so the volume halves.

qns_content.text: How much heat is required to convert \( 0.4 \, \text{kg} \) of ice at \( -25^\circ \text{C} \) to water at \( 50^\circ \text{C} \)? (Specific heat of ice = \( 2100 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \), latent heat of fusion = \( 3.35 \times 10^5 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \), specific heat of water = \( 4186 \, \text{J kg}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \))
Which temperature scale is based on the absolute minimum temperature where molecular activity theoretically ceases?

text_solutions: The Kelvin scale is defined with its zero point at absolute zero (\(-273.15^\circ \text{C}\)), the theoretical minimum temperature where molecular activity ceases, as per the ideal gas law and thermodynamic principles (Section 10.4).

qns_content.text: What determines the final temperature when two objects of different temperatures are mixed in a calorimeter?

text_solutions: The final temperature is determined by the principle of conservation of energy, where heat lost by the hotter object equals heat gained by the colder one, reaching thermal equilibrium.

qns_content.text: What defines the triple point of a substance?

text_solutions: The triple point is the unique temperature and pressure where solid, liquid, and vapor phases coexist in equilibrium (Section 10.8, Triple Point box).

Why does a substance with high specific heat capacity take longer to heat up?

options.text: It requires more heat per unit temperature rise

text_solutions: A high specific heat capacity means more heat (\( \Delta Q = m s \Delta T \)) is required per unit mass to raise the temperature, slowing the heating process (Section 10.6).
